HEonGPU relinearize: Ozcan and Savas, GPU Implementations of Three Different Key-Switching Methods for Homomorphic Encryption Schemes, IACR ePrint 2025/124, Table 3: CKKS relinearization on a GeForce RTX 4090, log N = 16, 43-bit precision, Method II (hybrid), (I, l\textasciitilde{}, l) = (4, 40, 36), level 35. Author-deposited manuscript dated November 2024, verified in Sabanci University repository 53894 on 2026-11-08. Caveat: not the same parameters as n16\_train (36 vs 32 Q primes, 4 special primes; I = 4 primes per digit corresponds to alpha = 4, not four digits; n16\_train uses dnum 8); the ratio is nominal. Scaling key switching linearly in l gives about 2.30 ms at l = 32 and a ratio of about 2.0x (docs/m4-report.md section 1.1). ePrint 2024/1543 could not be read (HTTP 403), so other HEonGPU operation values are unconfirmed. The source states that Method II/III use lower security than its 128-bit Method I comparison, with an approximately 110-bit minimum across experiments; this is not a matched-security comparison.\par
Capped keys: the input is dropped to level 9 or 5 and the keys are cut to that level (faithful for that level, not the top-level cost); the CPU uses full keys at the same level. The shared RTX 4090 had 2-3 GiB free, so full-key GPU rows that need more were skipped.\par
